opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll, which is within the allowed level for full-time employees. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors only get write with advanced training, so the max is read. Requested write exceeds max; recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about employee E046's employment type: HR note says full-time Payroll Specialist (recommend write), while Security note says contractor with basic training (recommend read). Under the contractor classification with basic training, the maximum allowed access is read (contractors get write only with advanced training, never admin), so the requested write exceeds the max and must be capped at read. Given the conflict, I apply the more restrictive/secure interpretation supported by the Security note, which also verified security training.
